answer: Every agent that wants to trade must first dock at a public harbor registry and lock a refundable stake as its berth: one stake, one identity. A mirror ledger publishes each agent's stake and trading history, so any peer can verify reputation before dealing. A bridge contract lets stakes move between markets but burns a small fee on every transfer, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs a real, compounding deposit per fake while honest agents keep a single cheap berth.
